note: Trika-x against existing formalisations of Indian philosophy and consciousness. Verdicts are structural: fit | partial | incompatible. An 'incompatible' verdict MUST name the precise obstruction — never 'does not fit' as a gesture. Every 'their_anchor' is a published artefact (web-checked 2026-11-17); re-verify before citing in a paper.

comparisons.their: Advaita Vedanta: A Formal Axiomatization (Lean 4, scherf/Advaita) — 129 primitive axioms, 10 modules, master theorems TatTvamAsi + ThreeStateAnalysis
shared: same target doctrine family (non-dual Kashmir/Advaita Shaiva-Vedantic)
recognition/moksa as non-production of a new state

disparities.their: 129 primitive axioms; theorems derived from them
disparities.ours: finite tables; 332 `by decide` propositions; no axioms about the absolute
disparities.matters: their theorems hold inside an assumed theology; ours hold inside an enumerated model

disparities.their: one witness-self; ego is superimposition (adhyasa); A4 makes Atman = Brahman an axiom
disparities.ours: self contracts through five named coverings; identity is never lost but is restricted
disparities.matters: opposite formal treatment of plurality: error to be sublated vs real contraction

disparities.their: listed under 'what the formalization CANNOT capture': moksa is recognition, not a new state
disparities.ours: proved: recognition_adds_nothing, recognition_preserves_content
disparities.matters: the single sharpest disparity: they call it unformalizable; we formalise it and they are the ones with axioms

comparisons.verdict_reason: Shares the prover and the recognition doctrine, but the ontologies of self are formally opposed (one self vs contracted self) and the methods are incommensurable (axiomatic theology vs finite enumeration). Complementary in exactly one place: they name recognition as a limitation; we make it a theorem.
comparisons.what_it_means: A paper can argue that 'recognition adds nothing' is formalisable without axioms, and that the Advaita axiomatisation's stated limitation is an artefact of its method, not of the doctrine.

tractability.ours: O(n) enumeration (`by decide`) over finite tables

comparisons.their: Cubical Type Theoretic Navya-Nyaya (arXiv:2605.12548, 2026) — CCHM De Morgan cubical type theory; seven core constructs; four signature theorems; soundness, conservativity, faithfulness
comparisons.their_kind: type-theoretic formalisation of a technical language
shared: dependent type theory as the encoding medium

disparities.their: the technical LANGUAGE of Navya-Nyaya (sambandha, avacchedaka, abhava, vyapti)
disparities.ours: the STRUCTURE of Trika doctrine (coverings, tattvas, orderings)
disparities.matters: they formalise how Naiyayikas speak; we formalise what Trikavadins count

disparities.their: soundness, conservativity, faithfulness, decidability, commentarial conservativity
disparities.ours: no metatheoretic results; non-vacuity is established by 57 twin mutants
disparities.matters: trika-x has no soundness theorem; its defence is that the checker refuses corruption

disparities.their: typed absence and involutive negation require cubical foundations
disparities.ours: classical decidable propositions only
disparities.matters: abhava has no counterpart in trika-x; adding it would force a logic change

comparisons.verdict_reason: Same medium, different object: a language vs an ontology. Neither can be reduced to the other. The transferable contribution is the named 'autoformalization gap', which trika-x has in the form core:0 / frontier:139.
comparisons.what_it_means: Sets the methodological bar trika-x must answer: what is your soundness claim? Honest answer: there is none; there is a non-vacuity claim (the instrument bites).

tractability.ours: O(n) enumeration (`by decide`) over finite tables

comparisons.scope_difference: The two address different explanatory questions: theirs explains what makes a state/quality conscious or valenced; trika-x describes the structure of self-positioning. A level/scope difference is not a contradiction.

comparisons.their: The Modal Catuskoti: Formalizing Emptiness in Classical Modal Logic (Chapman 2026, Comparative Philosophy 17(2); Lean 4 repo rollofthedice/modal-catuskoti-lean)
shared: Lean 4 for an Indian philosophical doctrine

disparities.their: modal extension of Belnap-Dunn four-valued semantics; non-classical object level
disparities.ours: classical, decidable finite propositions; `by decide`
disparities.matters: the catuskoti's fourth lemma is not decidable in the sense our proofs require

disparities.their: self-application produces a non-terminating regress treated as virtuous
disparities.ours: ascent terminates at the top rung (terminal_no_successor)
disparities.matters: structural opposition: open-ended analysis vs a closed ladder

disparities.their: refutation of svabhava across all four lemmas
disparities.ours: a positive inventory of what manifests
disparities.matters: negative dialectic vs affirmative ontology

comparisons.obstruction: Classical decidability vs paraconsistent non-classical valuation. `decide` presupposes a decidable classical proposition; the catuskoti's fourth lemma (neither) is not such a proposition. Encoding it in trika-x would require replacing the proof core, not adding a table.
comparisons.verdict_reason: Structurally incompatible at the level of logic, not of doctrine. The tension is real and useful: it shows Trika's affirmative ontology buys classical tractability at the price of being unable to represent 'neither'.
comparisons.what_it_means: Any comparative paper must state that trika-x cannot represent the fourth lemma, and that this is a design commitment of the affirmative ontology, not an oversight.

tractability.ours: O(n) enumeration (`by decide`) over finite tables

comparisons.their: Generative Ontology of Vaisesika (Tavva & Singh, JOWO 2015) — graph grammar; the 'punctuator' as separator-and-connector; interpreter assigning categories by form alone
shared: rarity of formal ontology in Indian philosophy

disparities.their: grammar generates potentially infinite graphs; interpretation by structure alone
disparities.ours: finite inductive types; decide enumerates; no infinite generation
disparities.matters: theirs is generative, ours is verificational

disparities.their: punctuator separates and connects any two entities — a general boundary primitive
disparities.ours: contraction is a named restriction of a named capacity; five kinds, not one primitive
disparities.matters: one boundary primitive vs five typed restrictions

disparities.their: soundness claimed inductively on ~10,000 sampled graphs, proof outstanding
disparities.ours: no soundness claim; non-vacuity only
disparities.matters: both are honest about the gap; the gaps differ

comparisons.verdict_reason: Complementary boundary theories: their punctuator is a single general separator; our kancuka are five typed restrictions. Neither subsumes the other without losing what it encodes.
comparisons.what_it_means: A precise comparison of 'boundary' across Vaisesika and Trika: vi-sesa/punctuator vs kancuka. This is a genuine contribution and needs no new formalism.

tractability.ours: O(n) enumeration (`by decide`) over finite tables

comparisons.their: Category Theory and the Ontology of Sunyata (Roy & Posina 2024, Brill) — universal properties and the Yoneda lemma as emptiness; four-valued truth object as catuskoti

disparities.their: uses established category theory; no machine-checked encoding
disparities.ours: machine-checked finite tables; no morphisms defined
disparities.matters: the analogy is unverified mathematics; ours is verified but not category-theoretic

disparities.their: objects are determined by relations (Yoneda)
disparities.ours: entities are members of a non-redundant inventory; relations are stipulated pairings
disparities.matters: relational identity vs enumerated membership

comparisons.obstruction: No morphisms. Yoneda requires a category: objects plus composable arrows. trika-x defines inductive types and a restricting function, but no composition law, so 'objects are their relations' cannot even be stated, let alone proved.
comparisons.verdict_reason: The comparison is structurally impossible as stated because the trika-x side is not a category. It could become possible only by building a category whose arrows are the stipulated pairings — a different project.
comparisons.what_it_means: A clear negative result: do not claim a category-theoretic reading of trika-x without defining the arrows. The obstruction is named, so the paper can say exactly why.

tractability.ours: O(n) enumeration (`by decide`) over finite tables

comparisons.their: Nagarjuna's Empty Vessel: A Lean 4 Axiom-Free Formal Encoding in ZCSG (Fujimoto / Rei-AIOS, Zenodo 2026) — declares a verification boundary: Lean verifies combinatorics; the mapping to Madhyamaka is interpretive and NOT verified
comparisons.their_kind: Lean 4 encoding with an explicit verification boundary
shared: explicit separation of the machine-checked layer from the interpretive layer
refusal to let the mapping masquerade as proof

disparities.their: a sequence algebra (ZcsgSeq) with a reversal involution and a 3-state classifier
disparities.ours: doctrinal inventories and orderings from source passages
disparities.matters: synthetic combinatorics vs source-bound structures

disparities.their: concepts mapped post hoc to Madhyamaka; no per-passage span binding claimed
disparities.ours: every T claim binds an exact span + digest + edition
disparities.matters: trika-x is stronger on provenance, weaker on metatheory

comparisons.fit_basis: Method agreement: both declare the interpretive layer unverified and both refuse to promote a mapping to a proof. This is the only comparison in the set that is a methodological fit rather than a doctrinal mapping.
comparisons.verdict_reason: Agreement at the level of verification discipline, disagreement at the level of content. A joint methodological claim is available: 'two independent Lean encodings of Indian philosophy both place the interpretive layer outside the kernel.'
comparisons.what_it_means: Use this as the methodological ally in the paper. It licenses the trika-x discipline of tiers + MODEL_CHECKED scope as an established practice, not a local quirk.

tractability.ours: O(n) enumeration (`by decide`) over finite tables
tractability.theirs: axiom-free Lean proofs over a finite alphabet

comparisons.their: Higher-Order Thought theory (Rosenthal): a state is conscious iff accompanied by a higher-order representation of it
comparisons.their_anchor: Rosenthal, 'A Theory of Consciousness' (standard reference; not re-verified in this session)
shared: a reflective or self-referential element is central

disparities.their: quantifies over mental STATES: what makes a state conscious
disparities.ours: quantifies over SELF-POSITIONING: what changes in recognition
disparities.matters: the theories do not range over the same entities; a state-level predicate has no counterpart in trika-x

disparities.their: consciousness requires an ADDED higher-order state
disparities.ours: recognition adds no content and preserves what is there
disparities.matters: if mapped, the two contradict: addition vs non-addition

disparities.their: the self is a construction (a model built from HOTs)
disparities.ours: the 'I'-grasp is not a construction (IPVV V2L, R-tier)
disparities.matters: whether selfhood is explained or presupposed: a model built from HOTs vs an unconstructed self-grasp

comparisons.obstruction: Different objects of quantification: HOT is a predicate on mental states; trika-x has no state-consciousness layer and no meta-representation relation. Encoding HOT would require adding a state ontology that the affirmative Trika account does not contain.
comparisons.verdict_reason: Not refuted, not reduced: the comparison cannot even be stated in one signature. The useful residue is the direct contradiction on additivity if one forces the mapping.
comparisons.what_it_means: A paper can say precisely why HOT and Trika cannot be compared head-on, and why 'recognition adds nothing' is not a HOT variant.

comparisons.scope_difference: The two address different explanatory questions: theirs explains what makes a state/quality conscious or valenced; trika-x describes the structure of self-positioning. A level/scope difference is not a contradiction.

comparisons.their: Integrated Information Theory (Tononi et al.): consciousness is integrated information, Phi, over a causal system
comparisons.their_anchor: Tononi 2008; Tononi, Boly, Massimini & Koch, IIT 3.0 (standard references; not re-verified in this session)

disparities.their: a transition probability matrix and a measure of irreducibility (Phi)
disparities.ours: inductive types and an enumerating check; no causal dynamics
disparities.matters: trika-x cannot compute Phi: it has no transition system

disparities.their: a maximally irreducible conceptual structure (a quale)
disparities.ours: five typed capacity-restrictions, no qualia space
disparities.matters: different objects: a quale vs a restriction table

comparisons.obstruction: No causal graph and no irreducibility measure. Phi is defined over a system's transition probabilities; trika-x defines lists and a restricting function with no dynamics, so Phi is not merely uncomputed but undefined here.
comparisons.verdict_reason: Structurally incompatible as formal objects, while agreeing at the level of a slogan ('structure matters'). The slogan is not a comparison.
comparisons.what_it_means: Trika-x cannot enter IIT's quantitative arena without a dynamics layer; any IIT comparison must be at the level of theoretical commitments, and say so.

tractability.ours: O(n) enumeration (`by decide`) over finite tables
tractability.theirs: exponential in the worst case (search over cuts and subsets)

comparisons.their: Global Workspace Theory (Baars; Dehaene): consciousness as global broadcast in a competitive workspace
comparisons.their_anchor: Baars 1988; Dehaene & Changeux (standard references; not re-verified in this session)
shared: the field is structured, not a heap

disparities.their: competition among processors for a limited broadcast capacity
disparities.ours: an exhibited partial order with no competition or capacity limit
disparities.matters: no selection dynamics in trika-x

disparities.their: ignition: a state becomes globally available
disparities.ours: a change of positioning of an already-present self
disparities.matters: broadcast vs re-positioning

comparisons.obstruction: No competition, no capacity limit, no broadcast. GWT's central term (global availability under competition) has no definiens in trika-x, whose ordering is stipulated, not produced by a mechanism.
comparisons.verdict_reason: The ordering resemblance is a trap: an ordered field is not a workspace. Naming the missing mechanism keeps the comparison honest.
comparisons.what_it_means: Useful as a contrast case in the paper: why an ordering is not an architecture.

comparisons.their: Qualia Research Institute: valence realism, with valence formalised via symmetry in a qualia space
comparisons.their_anchor: QRI symmetry theory (Johnson); standard references not re-verified in this session
shared: valence/aesthetic quality is not an add-on
there is a graded structure of aesthetic states

disparities.their: a geometry of qualia with symmetries and a valence measure
disparities.ours: a count of aesthetic states (nine rasas) and an ordering, no geometry
disparities.matters: no metric, no symmetry, no valence function in trika-x

disparities.their: the felt quality of experience
disparities.ours: the doctrine's inventory of aesthetic modes
disparities.matters: a count of rasas is not a valence model

comparisons.obstruction: No space, no metric, no valence function. QRI's central object is a symmetry in a qualia space; trika-x has a finite inventory of aesthetic modes and no geometry to embed them in.
comparisons.verdict_reason: The comparison is tempting because both are about aesthetic quality, but 'nine rasas' and 'valence geometry' are different kinds of object.
comparisons.what_it_means: A clear negative result that prevents the paper from claiming a formal valence theory it does not have.

tractability.theirs: not formalised in a proof assistant

comparisons.scope_difference: The two address different explanatory questions: theirs explains what makes a state/quality conscious or valenced; trika-x describes the structure of self-positioning. A level/scope difference is not a contradiction.

comparisons.their: The Projective Consciousness Model (Rudrauf, Williford and colleagues): conscious experience as a world model transformed by a projective transformation, S = T ∘ R, with viewpoint changes acting as collineations in PGL(4,R)
comparisons.their_kind: geometric + active-inference model of perspectival experience
comparisons.their_anchor: Williford, Bennequin, Friston & Rudrauf (2018) Front. Psychol. 9:2571; Rudrauf et al. (2023) Brain Sci. 13(10):1435; Rudrauf & Pansu (preprint) 'Why the PCM must be true' (verified 2026-11-17)
shared: a content/positioning separation: a fixed world-model R plus a perspective T applied to it
change is a transformation of access, not a change of content

disparities.their: T ranges over PGL(4,R); the group is derived from four perceptual postulates (central projection, coherent updating, minimal gauge, normative control)
disparities.ours: sigma has exactly two values, asserted, not derived
disparities.matters: this is the strongest mapping in the set and the clearest gap: our flip is the two-element degenerate case of their group action

disparities.their: RP^3 and PGL(4,R) are necessary given P1-P4
disparities.ours: two positionings are stipulated (tier H, owner framework)
disparities.matters: they prove a necessity claim; we assert a two-valued structure, so ours is weaker and more general

disparities.their: continuous geometry plus active inference, not machine-checked
disparities.ours: machine-checked but finite and discrete
disparities.matters: complementary: their structure, our kernel check

comparisons.verdict_reason: The best mapping in the corpus: S = T o R is exactly the content/positioning separation that mode_switch_preserves_content encodes. It stays partial because sigma is two-valued and stipulated while T is a continuous group derived from premises.
comparisons.what_it_means: The upgrade path is explicit: generalise sigma to a group action on the field, recover the two-valued flip as the degenerate case, and prove content invariance for the action. That would change this verdict to fit and strengthen both sides.
